text:
An approval screen tells you less than you think.

CERT-In reports an AI-assisted campaign targeting Indian financial entities through their payment interfaces. Its earlier advisory describes stolen credentials enabling direct payment calls that bypass application checks.

That is why I would look beyond the reassuring screen. The question is whether the system moving the money requires evidence of the approval, with the same recipient and amount attached.

If those details can change without another authorization, I would treat the approval as incomplete protection. A manager could approve one thing while the transfer mechanism accepts something else. That is a control gap worth understanding before trusting the display.

My takeaway: ask the business owner and IT lead to trace one approved payment all the way to transfer. Identify exactly what permission the final step accepts, and what stops a payment that differs from the approved record.

One trace cannot prove every payment is safe. It can test whether the confidence on screen has substance where money moves.
